- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, cap the increase at 2–3% above recent mean to avoid overreaction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (price moving back toward 70–72 range), adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next 5 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.3–0.7) and price is trending upward, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% to account for sentiment noise.  
- If forecast is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 5+ days, apply a downward bias correction of 0.5–1.0% per day to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts with sentiment >0.7, avoid predicting >+5% above 30-day moving average unless accompanied by strong policy or event signals.
